The trading strategy

The strategy looks for a low RSI as an entry opportunity. RSI compares recent gains and losses over 14 trading sessions. After each daily close, the program checks whether a selected asset’s RSI is below 35. At the first qualifying signal, it buys that asset at the next trading session’s open. Each asset is bought only once and held for the rest of the test; there are no sell orders or extra purchases.

Your starting capital is divided equally among the selected assets. Each portion stays in cash until its asset receives a buy signal. Once invested, that portion compounds at twice the asset’s daily open-to-open return, minus the financing and entry costs you set. The portions grow independently, so their shares of the portfolio change over time.

The chart compares the combined strategy with investing the same starting amount in SPY at 1× exposure from the beginning. A low RSI does not guarantee a price bottom, and 2× leverage magnifies both gains and losses.

Hypothetical results. Daily leverage doubles asset returns; broker margin calls and forced liquidation are not simulated.

How to read this test
  • Wilder RSI(14) is calculated on the shared trading dates after filtering the selected range. The first 14 price changes seed its gain/loss averages.
  • Each ticker is bought once, at the next session’s open after its first completed close with RSI below 35. Positions are held through the end. Later signals do not add positions.
  • Capital starts in equal independent cash sleeves. Active sleeves compound 2× daily open-to-open returns, less annual financing / 252 and leveraged entry costs. Sleeves are not rebalanced against each other. Cash earns no interest.
  • Each sleeve’s daily loss is capped at 100%. If all sleeves reach zero, the account remains at zero.
  • The benchmark is 1× SPY buy and hold, with a single unleveraged entry cost and no financing.
  • Returns use the intersection of all selected tickers’ dates. In-sample and out-of-sample are chronological labels on one continuous simulation; positions and RSI carry across the split. Metrics for each segment start from a value of 1.
  • The split includes the early RSI warm-up cash days, matching the latest Python code. Annualization uses 252 sessions. Positive days measures daily returns, not trade win rate.
  • RSI and position export columns retain the Python program’s timing: the row is dated at the next open; signal_date is one session before the interval’s starting open. Weight columns are gross exposure at the interval’s starting open and are recorded for every day, not only entry days.
  • Repeatedly tuning the rule to the held-back period removes its value as an untouched test. Results are hypothetical.
RSI(14) < 35 · One entry per asset · No sells · Equal starting sleeves · 2× daily leverage
